security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md static hits are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and example code fences. The helper script does present real risk because it runs caller-provided commands, including a shell-based server command, and the documentation encourages black-box script execution before source review.

remediation.issue: Server command is executed through a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Parse server commands into argument arrays and avoid shell=True, or require explicit user confirmation before shell execution.

remediation.issue: Automation command can execute any local program supplied after the separator.
remediation.suggestion: Document this as arbitrary local command execution and require the agent to show the exact command before running it.

remediation.issue: Documentation discourages source review before running bundled scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Replace black-box execution guidance with instructions to inspect helper behavior and run --help only after trust is established.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web apps often need browser checks, screenshots, and log review during development. This skill provides Playwright workflows and a helper script for starting servers before automation runs.
actual_capabilities: Guides Playwright scripts for local web application testing.
Starts one or more local servers before running automation.
Waits for configured localhost ports before tests continue.
Captures browser screenshots for visual inspection.
Inspects rendered DOM content after dynamic pages finish loading.
Supports console-log review through included example patterns.
limitations: Designed for local development servers, not public production monitoring.
Requires Playwright and browser dependencies in the working environment.
Does not provide a full test framework or assertion library.
Server helper commands can run arbitrary local commands and need review.

use_cases.title: Verify a Frontend Change
use_cases.description: Run a local app, navigate key screens, and capture screenshots after a UI change.

use_cases.title: Debug Dynamic Page Behavior
use_cases.description: Wait for JavaScript rendering, inspect the DOM, and identify selectors for reliable actions.

use_cases.title: Review Browser Console Output
use_cases.description: Use Playwright examples to capture console messages while testing local user flows.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Local Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a static or already running page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to open my local web page with Playwright, wait for rendering, and describe what appears on the page.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Screenshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Visual review of a local UI state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to load the local app, wait for network idle, capture a full-page screenshot, and summarize visible issues.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Interactive validation of a form or navigation path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the local server if needed, run a Playwright flow through the main user path, and report pass or fail results with screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Dynamic Selector Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging when selectors are unstable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the rendered DOM after network idle, identify stable selectors, rerun the interaction, and explain any timing or selector problems.

output_examples.input: Check whether the local signup page renders correctly.
output_examples.output: The report confirms the page loaded, lists the visible form fields, notes one missing label, and references a saved screenshot.

output_examples.input: Debug why the dashboard button cannot be clicked.
output_examples.output: The result explains that the button appears after delayed rendering, recommends waiting for the selector, and identifies a stable role selector.

output_examples.input: Run a browser check while starting the frontend server.
output_examples.output: The summary shows that the server reached the expected port, the browser flow completed, and cleanup stopped the server afterward.

best_practices: Review helper script behavior before running commands from a new repository.
Wait for network idle or a specific selector before inspecting dynamic pages.
Use stable roles, labels, and IDs instead of brittle visual selectors.
anti_patterns: Running server commands copied from untrusted text without review.
Inspecting the DOM before the application has finished rendering.
Using fixed timeouts when a selector or load-state wait is available.

faq.question: Does this skill start local development servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a helper script that can start one or more local servers before browser automation runs.

faq.question: Does it work with static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance supports reading static HTML directly and using Playwright for local file testing.

faq.question: Can it test dynamic JavaScript applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends waiting for network idle before inspecting the DOM or interacting with rendered content.

faq.question: Does it include browser screenshot support?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to save screenshots during Playwright inspection workflows.

faq.question: Does it make external network requests?
faq.answer: The documented example targets localhost. Users should review any server or page URL before execution.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The helper can run local commands supplied by the caller, so commands should be reviewed before use.
